properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/03/2023 to BIG DOG ENERGY LLC in Hempfield Twp, Westmoreland county. 78a64a(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Well site was not designed and constructed using secondary containment.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BIG DOG ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/03/2023
Violation Code: 78a64a(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Well site was not designed and constructed using secondary containment.
Violation ID: 981091
Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/03/2023
Comments: On January 3, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3435475 where violations were outstanding due to a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans, and no NOV response received from the operator. Also, no production reports had been submitted since 2014 per Department database, at the time of that inspection.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photo 1). No Emergency Response plans, or other required documents were onsite. No evidence of leaks or discharge could be found around the new production tanks, and they appeared to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they were not equipped with secondary containment (see photos 3 and 8). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the earthen berms surrounding these tanks, and at the bases of these tanks (see photos 4-7). The well tag and required operator's information was present on the meter box (see photo 8). The Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite. Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 10). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing.Based on observations from today's inspection, the violations that were continued in IR 3435475 shall remain outstanding, since no changes were made since and no NOV response has been received to date. An additional violation shall be issued against the production tanks, since they are not equipped with secondary containment in an unconventional site.

Comments: On site Monday (11/30/20) for the start up of Step Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs). There are (5) wells on this pad, they are the Hunter 5H, 6H, 21HC, 22HC and the 23HC. All (5) wells were in production. The (9x5), (13x9) and the (20x13) annuli of all the wells are plumbed to surface w/ rubber lines, the (20x13) annuli are venting to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and (9x5) annuli are sharing a 2" vent line to the production tanks. All annuli have transponders installed and are being monitored by the Operator. The ball valves were closed on all (20x13) annuli vents before there common vent line in order to isolate each annuli individually for gas checks being performed today for the beginning of the (SPBUTs).- Operator rep. (Tom Vitella) was on site to shut in the (20x13) annuli. - An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal.11/12/20) was turned on and gas checks performed @ the (20x13) Sentry valves showed no gas at time of shut in. - The (20x13) annuli were shut in @ 10:00, marking the start of the (SPBUTs). End of testing will be on Thurs. (12/3/20).

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Huntley & Huntley Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-10
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 879604
Permit API: 003-21903
Unconventional: No
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Frazer Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-03-02
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to inspection 2995415 conducted on 2/10/2020 in which sediment laden storm water was observed leaving the operators access road and entering a stream. Only the portion of the access road where the discharge was occurring is being inspected. PADEP Eric Norman is assisting and Operator representative Isaac Haky is on site. The access road appears to have been regraded and CFS put down on the road side ditch side of the access road. While the regrading has abated the accelerated erosion rills observed in previous inspections, the Department recommends that the operator stabilize the access road to prevent a reoccurrence. The operator appears to have laid down stone on the portion of the access road which was previously pooling water and no pooled water or discharges are observed at this time. Based on this observation the CSL violations will be closed as corrected/abated effective 3/2/2020. The operator has placed CFS on the road side ditch side of the access road, the CFS is not installed per the E&S Manual. The Department recommends that the operator install CFS per the E&S Manual detail 4-1. It appears that the rock laid at this location does not adequately cover the entire width of the access road leaving a strip on either side bare. The Department recommends that the operator stabilize these “shoulders” to prevent the possibility of accelerated erosion from occurring. Based on this inspection the CSL violations will be closed as corrected/abated. No new violations will be issued for this inspection. A follow up inspection for the other outstanding violations will be scheduled for a later date.

Comments: Incident inspection of Repsol's "Morgan 073" Marcellus well site.Harry Lammy (Repsol) called the DEP on Wednesday October 30, 2024 to report an estimated 20 gallon produced liquid release to the south end of the pad surface that day.Murray Kush (Repsol, Company Man) showed me where the produced liquid spill occurred when a vac truck overfilled on the south end of the pad surface near the gray cylindrical tanks. Gas Field Services removed the impacted pad material with guidance from Resource Management and placed it in an open top dumpster within 24 hours of the release. Soil in the remediated area has electrical conductivity of 0.02 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test meter. I did not observe any residual impacts from the spill. Violations for the spill are considered immediately corrected.Repsol expanded the flat pad area at this site February - May 2023. They spudded 4 new conductors on March 27, 2023. Precision Drilling 572 drilled the new wells into the Marcellus Shale in February-April 2024, adding to the existing 4 Marcellus wells at this site. Pro Frac hydraulically fractured the 4 new Marcellus wells here August 29-September 16, 2024. Repsol started flowing back liquid from the 4 new Marcellus wells on October 12, 2024 into the 37 tanks on the south end of the pad. They expect to finish flowback operations in about 1 week. Vegetation, rock, and erosion blanket stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Repsol constructed a new bioretention basin on the south end of the site, and removed the old basin.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface. Moist soil in 3 separate areas on the pad has electrical conductivity of 0.02-0.12 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test.Air temp 63FJLP

Comments: Incident inspection of Repsol's "Morgan 073" Marcellus well site.Harry Lammy (Repsol) called the DEP on Wednesday October 30, 2024 to report an estimated 20 gallon produced liquid release to the south end of the pad surface that day.Murray Kush (Repsol, Company Man) showed me where the produced liquid spill occurred when a vac truck overfilled on the south end of the pad surface near the gray cylindrical tanks. Gas Field Services removed the impacted pad material with guidance from Resource Management and placed it in an open top dumpster within 24 hours of the release. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/26/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 12/26/2026 in accordance with current regulations.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S Plan is present on site but has not been updated to depict streams and wetlands along the access road.- The entire length of the access road appears to have been graded, seeded, and mulched. - CFS remains improperly implemented or maintained at several points along the access road (Photos 3-8, 11-16, 19-21).- The outlet to Culvert 2 (Photo 12) and the inlet to Culvert 3 (Photo 13) remain blocked at this time.- Orange construction fence and CFS does not appear to have been installed along the access road where a wetland was identified by Department Biologists (Photo 22).- Sedimentation is observed at multiple points along the access road (Photos 6-7, 20-21).- Sedimentation at Culverts 5 and 8 appears to be threatening the stream, however no active discharge to the streams is observed at this time. - Regrading of the access road near the previous location of the production tank appears to have resulted in sediment being pushed to the end of the access road, which appears to be currently held by brush. Comments On 4/1/2014, I conducted an inspection of the Atlas Resources DEIDRICH # 3 OG WELL well in Jefferson Township, Fayette County. The inspection was the result of Atlas reporting a brine spill of unknown quantity, some of which went off containment at this site. Atlas reported the spill to me on 3/31/14. On 4/3/2014, Atlas submitted an Initial Spill/Incident Notification to the Department. According to reports from Atlas, the spill was thought to be the result of a leaking 3" valve and a hole in the 100 barrel tank. The brine leaked out of the tank and caused a puddle of brine inside secondary containment. The containment dike had a drain pipe with a cap. Recent precipitation events caused the fluid in the dike to overflow it's banks. A small amount of brine left the site onto the access road and killed a small amount of vegetation below the road. The area of dead vegetation was approximately 2 foot by 2 foot. The leaking tank will be replaced by a poly tank and the operator has cleaned up the affected soil and performed testing to ensure all Brine water leaked out of hole in tank and leaking 3" valve into containment and also went outside containment.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/17/2026 to MCCOOL JOHN E in Cherry Grove Township, Warren county. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: MCCOOL JOHN E
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/17/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8278642
Permit API: 123-47075
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Cherry Grove Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/17/2026
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to the observation of production fluid exiting the secondary containment of the Lot 740 tank battery. Conventional well Lot 740 15 (API # 123-47075) is nearest the tank battery. The conventional well appears to be plumbed for production. An old sign displaying the API number, well name, and the wrong operator contact information is posted on a tree near the location. The sign should be updated with the current operator's name and contact information. The tank battery at the site has 2 steel tanks and a separator situated within an earthen secondary containment. The secondary containment was approximately 60ft x 20ft. Evidence of staining, dead vegetation, numerous deer tracks, and conductivity readings over range (greater than 20,000 mS/cm maximum that field meter can measure) were present in standing water throughout the entire secondary containment. This would indicate a large volume of production fluid filled the entire containment at one time (see photo 1). At the time of the inspection, the ground within the secondary containment was saturated with production fluid with some ponding throughout. A small amount of crude oil was also identified within the escaped production fluid. A containment drain inlet was located at a low point in the front left corner within the containment. A conductivity reading of 17.17 mS/cm was measured at the drain inlet (see photo 2). The ponding production fluid was flowing into the drain's inlet, exiting the containment through the drain outlet located at the exterior front left corner of the secondary containment (see photo 3). The containment drain was open and unattended at the time of this inspection. Sample 001 was collected at 13:10 at the containment drain outlet for further testing. A conductivity reading was also taken at this location measuring over range (see photo 4). The production fluid flowed from the containment drain into the road ditch traveling south approximately 50 feet (see photo 5). The escaped production fluid also flowed north in the road ditch approximately 10 feet before entering a road culvert where it continued westward into the woods for approximately 150 feet (see photo 6). The vegetation in the path of flow was dead, the ground was muddy and imprinted with deer tracks, and the conductivity readings measured high throughout the entire length of travel. The conductivity was measured near the apparent end of impact with a reading of 8.51 mS/cm in a puddle.The containment drain is required to be closed when unattended and the regulations state that any discharge is to only consist of precipitation that accumulates inside the containment, not production fluids. On June 18, 2026 a phone call was made to the operator, John McCool, in which he stated his intentions to work towards achieving compliance. He explained that the fluids currently stored in the tanks will be pumped empty and examined for leaks. If any leaks are identified, the tanks will be repaired or replaced. An excavator will be used to remove the contaminated soil within the secondary containment and beyond the containment drain exit following the path of travel through the woods. Upon disposing of the contaminated soils at an approved facility, a copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department. Confirmatory sampling will be required to confirm the impacts from the release have been sufficiently remediated. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites and Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/06/2025
Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8232915
Permit API: 051-22343
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Luzerne Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/06/2025
Comments: On May 6, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a complaint at the Whiteko 4 well site in Luzerne Township, Fayette County.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag and no staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around it (see photos 3 and 4). The operator's information is posted on the meter box (see photo 7). Staining was observed on the ground underneath the meter box (see photos 8 and 13). However, this staining may be caused by algae growth due to no elevated conductivity and a moss-like odor exhibited in this location (see photo 8). No petroleum odor or residue was observed in this stained area. Some rust was observed on brine tank, however it appears to be sound at the time of inspection. Standing rainwater was observed in the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank. The conductivity level of this standing water underneath the brine tank valve was not indicative of a brine fluid leak (see photo 12 and 13). The well site appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1 and 5). Tire rutting that varies in severity was observed in the access road and low-hanging vegetative overgrowth was observed that appears to be capable of hindering vehicular access to the well site in the event of an emergency (see photos 14-16 and 19). The tire rutting was most severe near the entrance of the access road that also made vehicular access to the site difficult. What appears to be a steep third-party road was observed that intersects with the access road. A deep erosion rill was observed going downslope perpendicular to the access road that appears to be capable hindering vehicular access to the well site in the event of an emergency and resulting in accelerated erosion and sedimentation (see photos 17 and 18).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the operator clear the low-hanging vegetative overgrowth along the access road to ensure a clearance height that continues to permit vehicular access to site.Violations shall be issued against the tire rutting and deep erosion rill in the access road, as it appears that it may hinder vehicular access to the well site and result in accelerated erosion and sedimentation onsite.

Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 8173124
Permit API: 129-28930
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Salem Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/25/2024
Comments: On January 25 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Fatur Well Pad after a Department OGI requested a follow up in regards to a pink oily substance observed on the pad.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The Act 9 sign was present at the time of the inspection, and appeared to be in good condition. The ERP and PPC plans were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head at the time of this inspection. There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible leaks. Upon inspection of the GPU, there appeared to be a red tinted fluid in the containment surrounding the GPU. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid with in the containment and revealed elevated readings of 4.39mS. Upon further inspection, there appeared to be a disconnected hose and red tinted fluid on the gravel behind the GPU. Conductivity readings were taken from the surface on the ground beneath the puddles on the well pad and indicated elevated readings of 1.08mS and 1.37mS in comparison to the background reading of 0.12 mS taken from the surface of the soil along the well site perimeter. Directly adjacent to the GPU was a container with red colored fluid labeled as gear lubricant. The Department recommends the operator assess the red tinted fluid observed on the ground near the GPU as well as inside of the containment and remediate any spills in accordance with Department standards. The Department requests clarification on what the red tinted fluid observed on the ground is and how much was released with in 10 days of receiving this report.Upon inspecting the additional production equipment onsite, there appeared to be oil based matter being absorbed by cloths beneath the compressor. There did not appear to be any staining on the ground surrounding the compressor. The Department recommends the operator ensure the structural integrity of the all production equipment is sound and properly contain and dispose of any production related fluid in the proper manner to prevent any future pollution events. Upon inspection of the area mentioned by an OGI to have a pink oily matter on the ground, it appeared that a majority of the substance may have been washed away by recent rain as only small spots of a pink colored matter was observed on the ground surrounding a production tank next to the compressor. Conductivity readings were taken on the ground where the pink substance was observed and did not indicate elevated reading with readings of 0.13mS and 0.11mS. Upon inspection of the production tank and containment, the pink oily fluid was observed. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid with in the containment and did not indicate elevated readings with a reading of 0.09mS. The Department requests information regarding what was released and how much was released in this area with in 10 days of receipt of this report. The Department recommends removing excess fluids from secondary containments in order to ensure they meet required holding capacities of 110% according to Chapter 78a64a.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the release observed near the GPU, failure to have the gear lubricant in proper secondary containment, and the secondary containment for the production tank near the compressor failing to meet proper storage capacity. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of operator response.

Comments: On 02/14/2024, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Hixenbaugh 1-P060 well. I notified Joel Greco of KPI ("operator"), regarding my findings on 02/14/2024. It was noted that there was rig work recently conducted onsite and that there were some things to address/clean up. The following was observed during the inspection:Well tags displaying the well and operators information were noted on site (Photos 1, 2).A methanol drum was noted on site. Although not required, I recommended placing containers within secondary containment to avoid substances from reaching the ground. Mr. Greco noted that the drum was empty and used for tubing that was experiencing freezing/thawing issues. I recommend that any unnecessary material is removed from the site and disposed of properly (Photos 3-5). In a 06/16/2017 compliance evaluation inspection (Inspection Report 2614040), a methanol drum was noted onsite without secondary containment and a violation of 91.34(a) was issued on 09/20/2016 (Inspection Report 2532594, Enforcement 348270).There was a spot of grease-like material on the ground near the tubing. The area is relatively small, however, I recommend that this is remediated and disposed of at an approved waste facility (Photos 4, 5). A section of grease-like material was noted along the tarp beside the oil tank. Although not required, secondary containment is recommended to be used to avoid any substances from reaching the ground (Photos 6-8). The operator explained that maintenance was being performed on the compressor station. Oil/grease material was noted within the trough along the compressor (Photos 9, 10). A grease-like material was noted around the wellhead. The wellhead and production equipment were in generally good condition. A splattered substance was noted on the production equipment; however, this may be paint. Monitoring recommended (Photos 11-13).The earthen berm around the production tank was in generally good condition and vegetated. Possible third-party disturbance and activity were noted near the production tank (Photos 14, 15). Several spots around the base of the production tanks displayed a grease/oil-like material on the tank and the ground. Petroleum crude oil noted on tanks right to know label. I recommend the removal of this material from the ground and cleaning off the tank. I also recommend lifting the tank to ensure no material is underneath. Marks from a material moving down the side of the tank were noted, most likely from precipitation (Photos 16-20). Violations were noted at this site on 09/20/2016 (Inspection Report 2532594, Enforcement 348270) regarding oil/grease within the earthen berm around the production tank. The access road was in relatively okay condition. No active E and S issues were noted; however, this road may be prone to accelerated erosion. I recommend routine maintenance of the access road (Photos 21-23). Several areas around the site displayed oil/grease on the ground. I recommend that each area be addressed, and the waste delivered to an approved waste facility. The Department is requesting that a waste manifest be submitted as soon as possible. Due to the discovery of grease/oil on the ground, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 91.34(a) are being issued.

Comments: Site inspection conducted at the COP Tract 551B pad to review use of EWS VOX4 evaporators for processing flowback water. Meeting on site today with EWS representative Pat Pascarella. There are no EQT personnel on site at time of inspection. A TetraTek crew is loading produced fluid into water trucks. Weather conditions are partly sunny and 73 degrees F. Wind is blowing from the southwest at an estimated 5 mph. Eight EWS Vox4 evaporators are in use at time of inspection. Evaporators process fluid in batches, with automated systems in use to pump water into the system from the production fluid tanks and out to the frac tank batteries when fluid is concentrated. All pipelines and fluid control systems appear to be functioning as designed and there is no fluid or precipitation within evaporator containment. As authorized under the Air Quality Request for Determination Operating Permit, EQT will take four evaporators out of service after the initial 60 days of use. According to Mr. Pascarella, four units will be disconnected on June 13. There are no violations associated with the evaporator authorization. Fluid with elevated conductivity (3.14 mS/cm) is still present at the NE pad sump (photo 7). Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/08/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in Cascade Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/08/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 987579
Permit API: 081-21907
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/08/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up after the operator reported that on 3/3/23, an estimated 50 barrels of produced fluid was released on and off of secondary containment. The area surrounding the well pad and access road was snow-covered during this inspection. DEP Water Quality Specialist Supervisor Sean VanFleet accompanied me during this inspection. The frac was on-going during this inspection. Company man Matt Casler accompanied us at the beginning of the inspection in order to show us the location of the produced fluid release from 3/3/23. The area where the fluid released sprayed onto the pad surface is the area east of the modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) and the travel lane which runs along the southcentral edge of the pad. According to the company man, approximately 4 inches of material was scraped from the surface of the pad in these areas and had been hauled off site. No fluid was observed in this area. Mr. Casler also stated that no fluid or staining was observed on the south pad side slope immediately after the release. No fluid or staining was observed on the pad side slope or at the toe of the slope during this inspection.At the north corner of the pad at the outlet of the stormwater channel, the stormwater has an electrical conductivity (EC) of approximately 440 uS/cm. In the secondary containment at the west corner of the pad, adjacent to the MASS, fluid is present with an EC of 6.25 mS/cm. The produced fluid offload area at the southeast corner of the pad has fluid within it which has an EC of 3.00 mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming out these containments. Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release which occurred on 3/3/23.

On 02/27/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of the Wygrala Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. Pooled fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 188-721 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment. There were several temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment. Recovered material was being removed from the site during the inspection (photo #9). Comments: On 03/22/19 - 10:30: Lower Reno 4A 121-44422 was observed pumping. The production line from this well is buried and travels underground to a separator located near Lower Reno 1 A 121-44463. From the separator, the oil line is buried and travels down gradient to the production tanks. The brine line runs on the surface down gradient. The fittings on the brine line from the separator are showing signs of corrosion and are occasionally dripping onto the ground. It appears there has been a previous discharge in the area by the appearance of the dead vegetation. The brine line was followed down gradient and observed discharging at 41.421803 N, -79.768843 W. At the spot the discharge was occurring the line was separated at a hose nipple. There is a large area of dead vegetation at the discharge location. When the well was pumping a substantial amount of fluid was observed discharging. On this date a sample could not be collected, and further investigation will take place. 03/27/19 - 09:45 The area where the flow line was previously discharging was inspected and found to be discharging. A sample was collected (0641-119). The flow rate during sampling was much slower then observed on 03/22/19. After the sample was collected it was observed that no wells were currently pumping. The operator was called (Harry Rhodes) and notified of the violation. The Department will meet with the operator on 04/02/19. The operator was advised that he should shut the lease down to cease the discharge. Violations are noted.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Terry Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-19
Comments: Weather was 59° and cloudy. Met with Chesapeake representative Tim Long on location. Well was recently drilled to TD and all casing strings were set and cemented. Well was currently shut in. After well drilling was completed, bubbling was noticed inside the cellar. The cellar was pumped down and it was discovered that the bubbling was from a leak in the surface casing cap.
